citation.title: TopoCtrl: Post-Optimization Topology Editing Toward Target Structural Characteristics
citation.authors: Hongrui Chen, Dat Ha, Josephine V. Carstensen, Faez Ahmed
citation.version_coded: arXiv v1 (27 Mar 2026; only version on the abs page), full text read from https://arxiv.org/html/2603.26926

claim.primary_outcome_paraphrase: Across 100 OAT test topologies, best-of-64 TopoCtrl edits reached 83.84–99.50% of the target characteristic ranges, versus 16.94–56.00% for re-running topology optimization with seven filter radii (Table 2).
claim.key_phrase: broader reachable characteristic coverage than the benchmark based on varying the filter radius
claim.location: Section 4.2, Table 2 (first quantitative classical comparison; abstract, conclusion and introduction compare only qualitatively)
claim.claimed_speedup_basis: No classical runtime is reported. Only TopoCtrl inference (about 0.5 s per sample) and regressor training (about 3 min per characteristic) are given (Sec. 4). Not derivable.
claim.alternatives: (1) Abstract, qualitative: edits are said to keep the original layout and the designer's intent better than tuning solver parameters or applying simple geometric edits; no geometric-edit baseline appears in Sec. 4. (2) Abstract, cost proxy: no per-characteristic re-derivation of the problem or its sensitivities and no iterative re-solve is needed; not quantified, no classical time reported. (3) Table 2 at best-of-64 vs the filter-radius benchmark: volume-fraction error 0.03–0.10% vs 0.21%, IoU 79.21–84.93% vs 76.45%.

baseline.classical_method: Re-running the conventional TO solver that generated the OAT dataset on each test problem with the filter radius varied from 1.5 to 12, 7 reruns per topology (Sec. 4.2, Fig. 6); the TO formulation is not described in this article
baseline.hardware_ml: PC with an RTX Pro 6000 GPU, 96 GB VRAM (Sec. 4)
baseline.problem_size: OAT test-set problems of varying domain size and aspect ratio; grid resolution not stated in this article; 100 test topologies (Sec. 4)
baseline.ml_time: about 0.5 s per sample on average; 64 samples per topology-target pair (Sec. 4)
baseline.training_time: about 3 min per characteristic regressor (Sec. 4); OAT pretraining cost not stated
baseline.data_generation_cost: not stated; regressors trained on a 150K-sample subset of the OAT pretraining set labelled by medial-axis analysis (Sec. 4)
baseline.quality_metric: Coverage of the prescribed characteristic interval (Eq. 18), volume-fraction error (VFE), IoU with the original topology, failure rate = share of edits with compliance above 2× the ground-truth topology (Table 2)
baseline.quality_gap: Best-of-64 coverage vs benchmark (BM): joints 94.82% vs 23.89%; members per joint 99.50% vs 56.00%; length 83.84% vs 43.80%; thickness 85.02% vs 16.94%. TopoCtrl failure rate 4.67–16.00% at best-of-64 and 38.67–49.00% at best-of-2; BM failure rate N/A (Table 2)

R1.evidence: Table 2 and Sec. 4.2: TopoCtrl best-of-N (N = 2-64 samples per topology-target pair, 16 target settings) vs 7 TO reruns per topology with filter radius 1.5-12. Volume is matched (VFE 0.03-0.10% vs 0.21% at best-of-64). Structural performance is not matched: TopoCtrl failure rates (compliance above 2× the original) are 4.67-16.00% at best-of-64, the BM failure rate is not reported, and compliance values are not tabulated. Neither the compute budget nor the TO stopping rule is stated.

R2.evidence: Primary outcome is controllability coverage only; no classical runtime is reported and no speed claim is quantified, so the efficiency criteria (a)-(e) do not apply.

R3.evidence: No quantified speed claim against a classical method. For C3: regressor training (about 3 min per characteristic) and inference (about 0.5 s per sample) are reported (Sec. 4); OAT pretraining and OAT dataset-generation costs are not reported.

R4.evidence: Sec. 4.2 and Table 2: characteristics are recomputed on the decoded topologies with the same medial-axis evaluator (not the regressor); failure rate (compliance above 2× ground truth, following the OAT protocol; FE-based [inferred]) and VFE are reported for every N; the best-of-N selection rule is stated. Qualitative figures show selected examples, but the quantitative results cover all 100 test topologies.

reporting.n_test_cases: 100 OAT test topologies × 16 target settings over 4 characteristics, 64 samples each; plus one cantilever beam (Sec. 4, 4.3)

notes: Screening code was I-SPEED; full text gives stratum Q (I-QUALITY) because the first quantitative classical comparison (Table 2, coverage vs filter-radius TO reruns) concerns controllability, and no classical runtime is reported anywhere. The abstract's comparison with simple geometric edits has no matching experiment in Sec. 4. Sec. 4.2 says Table 2 reports compliance, but the table holds only the failure rate. Sec. 5 notes that fewer than 64 samples give insufficient accuracy. Reporting locators: n = Sec. 4; OOD = Sec. 4.3 (cantilever beam, qualitative only); failure rate = Table 2 (TopoCtrl only); timing and hardware = Sec. 4 (ML side only); code = GitHub link at the end of Sec. 1. Repository page read 2026-09-24: public demo (cantilever notebook), no licence file identified, README points to Hugging Face for the model checkpoints, no scripts for Table 2 or the filter-radius baseline. No data availability statement in the article. retest_candidate false: no speed claim to re-test and the benchmark scripts are not provided.
